new_questions.title: Best undergraduate CS programs (US News)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the US News Best Undergraduate Computer Science ranking (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: Ranking based solely on peer-assessment scores from deans and senior CS faculty at accredited schools. Ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: The 'Big Four' of undergraduate CS — MIT, Stanford, CMU, and Berkeley — have shared the peer-assessment top spot at a perfect 5.0 for years, well ahead of the field.
new_questions.source_name: US News & World Report — Best Undergraduate Computer Science Programs

new_questions.title: Best undergrad engineering programs (US News)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the US News Best Undergraduate Engineering ranking for schools whose highest engineering degree is a doctorate (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: US News undergraduate engineering ranking, doctorate-granting category. Peer-assessment-based; ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: MIT has held the top spot in this category continuously in the modern rankings era, with Stanford and Berkeley usually filling the next two slots.
new_questions.source_name: US News & World Report — Best Undergraduate Engineering Programs (Doctorate)

new_questions.title: Best law schools (US News)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the US News Best Law Schools ranking (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: US News Best Law Schools ranking for JD programs. Ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: Yale Law held the #1 US News law school spot every year from 1987 through 2023 — the longest continuous #1 streak of any US News professional-school ranking. Stanford tied and then edged past it in the most recent rankings.
new_questions.source_name: US News & World Report — Best Law Schools

new_questions.title: Best medical schools — Research (US News)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the US News Best Medical Schools — Research ranking (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: US News Best Medical Schools — Research ranking. Weights NIH research funding, peer assessment, and residency-director assessment. Ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: Harvard Medical School has held the #1 US News research-medical-school spot in every ranking since the list first appeared in 1990.
new_questions.source_name: US News & World Report — Best Medical Schools: Research

new_questions.title: Highest total R&D expenditures (NSF HERD)
new_questions.prompt: Name the US universities that spent the most on research and development in the most recent NSF Higher Education R&D (HERD) survey.
new_questions.disclaimer: Total R&D expenditures include federal, state, industry, institution, and foundation funding. Multi-campus UC / UT systems reported per-campus in NSF HERD; UCSF is excluded from this list because it is a health-sciences-only campus not in our institution set. Values in USD.
new_questions.trivia: Johns Hopkins has led NSF HERD by a wide margin for over 40 straight years — driven overwhelmingly by the Applied Physics Laboratory, a federally funded R&D center in Laurel, MD.
new_questions.source_name: National Science Foundation — Higher Education Research & Development (HERD) Survey FY2023

new_questions.title: Forbes America's Top Colleges (2024)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the Forbes America's Top Colleges 2024 ranking (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: Forbes weights alumni salary, student debt, graduation rate, Forbes American Leaders List membership, and retention. Ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: Forbes was the first major outlet to rank US colleges primarily on outcome data — salary, debt, career achievement — rather than reputation and inputs, launching its list in 2008.

new_questions.title: WSJ Best Colleges in America (2024)
new_questions.prompt: Name the highest-ranked schools in the Wall Street Journal / College Pulse Best Colleges in America ranking (rank 1 = best).
new_questions.disclaimer: WSJ / College Pulse ranking weights student outcomes (salary impact, graduation rate) at ~70%, plus learning environment and diversity. Ties share a rank.
new_questions.trivia: The WSJ methodology weights salary-impact-above-expected far more than US News does — a big reason Princeton and MIT typically top this list ahead of Harvard.
new_questions.source_name: Wall Street Journal / College Pulse — Best Colleges in America

new_questions.title: Best US MBAs (Financial Times Global MBA)
new_questions.prompt: Name the US business schools ranked highest in the Financial Times Global MBA ranking (rank 1 = best US school).
new_questions.disclaimer: Restricted to US business schools; ranks reflect their position among US schools in the FT Global MBA ranking. Weights alumni salary three years after graduation, salary increase, career progress, diversity, and research output.
new_questions.trivia: The FT ranking is the only major MBA ranking that weights research output heavily, which is why long-time academic powerhouses like Wharton and Booth reliably rank near the top ahead of purely brand-driven programs.

new_questions.title: Most VC-backed startup founders (PitchBook)
new_questions.prompt: Name the US universities whose undergraduate programs have produced the most VC-backed startup founders.
new_questions.disclaimer: Counts undergraduate alumni who founded venture-capital-backed companies. PitchBook Universities Rankings. Restricted to US universities.
new_questions.trivia: Berkeley overtook Stanford as the #1 US undergrad-founder factory in PitchBook's 2023 rankings — powered by its massive College of Engineering and lower cost of attendance than the Ivies + Stanford.

new_questions.title: Most US utility patents granted
new_questions.prompt: Name the US universities that were granted the most US utility patents in the most recent National Academy of Inventors annual report.
new_questions.disclaimer: Counts US utility patents granted to universities as assignee in the most recent calendar year. Multi-campus university systems (e.g. University of California, University of Texas) are aggregated by the source and excluded here so single-campus universities can be compared directly.
new_questions.trivia: MIT alone has been granted more US patents in recent years than any Ivy League university except one (Harvard) — a legacy of its long-standing bench-to-market translation pipeline.
new_questions.source_name: National Academy of Inventors — Top 100 Worldwide Universities Granted US Utility Patents
